extracted.intended_audience: immigration practitioners and stakeholders (immigration lawyers, advocacy/immigrant advocacy groups, non-profits, healthcare providers, NGOs), regulated entities, and DHS rule commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed DHS regulation defining and implementing the public charge ground of inadmissibility, including definitions, required factors, weighing approach, valuation of benefits, exemptions/waivers, bond processes, forms and fee changes, and procedural requirements for admissions/adjustments/changes of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory mandatory factors for public charge determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute requires DHS to consider the following minimum factors that reflect the likelihood that an alien will become a public charge: the alien’s age; health; family status; assets, resources, and financial status; and education and skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS will evaluate these as the minimum mandatory factors under INA section 212(a)(4)(B)(i). The rule also states DHS may consider any affidavit of support submitted by the alien’s sponsor and any other factor relevant to the likelihood of the alien becoming a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective, totality-of-the-circumstances determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that evaluating public charge is a prospective determination based on the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination considers current and future circumstances; positive and negative factors are weighed together to determine whether an individual is likely at any time in the future to become a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of key terms (public charge, public benefit, likely to become a public charge, household)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish key definitions, including public charge, public benefit, likely to become a public charge, and household.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulation provides specific regulatory definitions to guide adjudicators on the scope of benefits and who is subject to the public charge inadmissibility determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of affidavit of support (Section 213A) as a factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Any affidavit of support submitted under section 213A of the Act may be considered in the public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit of support is required for many family-sponsored (and some employment-sponsored) immigrants; an applicant without a sufficient affidavit of support may be inadmissible. When required, applicants must submit Form I-864 (Affidavit of Support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of both cash and non-cash public benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes the previous distinction between cash and non-cash benefits and allows consideration of receipt of non-cash public benefits when determining whether an applicant meets the definition of 'public charge.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns public charge policy with PRWORA self-sufficiency principles by treating cash and non-cash benefits consistently rather than focusing only on primary dependence on cash benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlining minimum and additional factors; positive and negative factor weighing
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlines minimum and additional factors considered when evaluating whether an alien is inadmissible as likely to become a public charge; positive and negative factors are weighed to determine likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule sets out a structured list of factors (minimum and additional) and instructs adjudicators to weigh these factors under the totality-of-the-circumstances approach rather than apply a single-factor rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation methodology for monetizable benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides the methodology for calculating the value of the benefit attributable to the alien in proportion to the total number of people covered by the benefit in the public charge inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation defines how to apportion the monetary value of public benefits for use in assessing the applicant’s likelihood of becoming a public charge (i.e., proportionate allocation when benefits cover multiple people).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of exempt categories and waiver eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlines exemptions and waivers for inadmissibility based on public charge grounds and proposes to list exempt immigrant and nonimmigrant categories in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule will enumerate applicants not subject to the public charge ground and those eligible to apply for waivers; adjudicators should follow the regulatory lists when determining applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge bond process and discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets forth the Secretary’s discretion to approve public charge bonds, cancellation, bond schedules, and breach, and moves principles governing public charge bonds to proposed 8 CFR 213.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a discretionary process under which USCIS could offer public charge bonds to otherwise admissible applicants found inadmissible only on public charge grounds, including minimum bond amounts and administrative requirements. The rule notes USCIS would need a unit to administer the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and costs associated with bonds and new forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds fees for new Form I-945 (Public Charge Bond) and Form I-356 (Request for Cancellation of Public Charge Bond); anticipates fees paid to surety bond companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies estimated costs (e.g., $0.34 million annually to obligors for Form I-945; $825 annually to filers for Form I-356) and notes surety fees could range from 1–15 percent of the bond amount based on an individual’s credit score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for nonimmigrant extension/change of status applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes that, with limited exceptions, an application for extension of stay or change of nonimmigrant status will be denied unless the applicant demonstrates that he or she has not received, is not currently receiving, nor is likely to receive, public benefits as defined in proposed 8 CFR 212.21(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although section 212(a)(4) does not directly apply to extensions/changes of status, DHS proposes applying a self-sufficiency requirement for these applicants to ensure they continue to be self-sufficient for the duration of their temporary stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of status evidence requirement (Form I-944 declaration of self-sufficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends 8 CFR 245 to require that aliens submit a declaration of self-sufficiency on the form designated by DHS (Form I-944) and any other evidence requested by DHS in the public charge inadmissibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule specifies an increased documentation burden for adjustment applicants, including a required self-sufficiency declaration and potential RFEs requesting additional evidence; DHS estimates time burdens and costs associated with completing Form I-944.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-sufficiency policy principle and sponsor support standard
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS’s view of self-sufficiency: aliens subject to the public charge ground must rely on their own capabilities and support from family, sponsor, and private organizations rather than seek public benefits; sponsors must provide support under section 213A at not less than 125 percent of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy orientation informs adjudications and regulatory design; immediate relatives and many family-preference immigrants require legally binding affidavits of support showing sponsor income at ≥125% of FPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicator discretion and historical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reaffirms that public charge determinations involve the exercise of adjudicator discretion and references prior administrative decisions that public charge analysis considers all factors bearing on ability/potential to be self-supporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule builds on precedent (e.g., Matter of Vindman) and directs adjudicators to consider varied elements (financial status, health, employability, family support) within their discretionary authority rather than apply a rigid definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory restructuring and CFR amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds and amends specific CFR provisions (e.g., adding 8 CFR 212.20–212.24; amending 8 CFR 214.1, 248.1, 245, 103.6, 103.7, 213.1) to implement the proposed policies, processes, fees, and bond rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table and narrative describe the purpose and expected impact of each CFR change, the procedural and substantive requirements tied to those provisions (e.g., definitions, valuation, exemptions, bond mechanics, forms and fees).
